subject: Clearsky — dedicated capacity sizing and GPU options (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Nora Bennett <nora@clearsky.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@clearsky.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap + next steps: dedicated capacity sizing for low-latency streaming

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. Per our ask: I wanted to capture the performance targets we discussed, call out open data we need from you, and propose a short validation plan for dedicated capacity sizing and GPU options.

Summary of what I heard you say (please correct if I misremember):
- Goal SLO: p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 250ms for typical interactive completions (avg response length ~120 tokens).
- Typical request shape: short prompts, 32–64 token prompts, ~80–150 token completions (we asked for actual histograms — see attachment).
- Peak concurrency: ~300–400 simultaneous active users (concurrent open streams); peak sustained QPS expected ~20–30 req/s across service during spikes.
- Business willingness: start with reserved capacity (monthly) for predictable tail behavior, expand after initial validation.

Open items we need from you to size:
1) Representative sample of request/response token lengths (CSV attached is fine).
2) Peak sustained requests-per-second during business hours vs peak spikes (15-min window).
3) Any network egress constraints or proxy termination that will add ms to the RTT.

Redwood recommended validation approach (high level):
- Synthetic perf run using your sample payloads (we replay at target concurrency and at 25/50/100% above to find inflection points).
- Test matrix: cold-start latency, steady-state p50/p95/p99, streaming tail-latency with 256-token sessions, and KV/prefix cache effectiveness.
- GPU options to compare: H100 (best tail and KV memory), A100 80GB (balanced), L40 (cost-efficient, good for int8). We'll size two configs and recommend reserved pool accordingly.

Proposed next steps:
- Nora/Samir: share the CSV + any ACLs for a one-time log sample (attachment preferred) by EOD Wed.
- Redwood: schedule a 3-hour perf run Thu/early Fri (we can do multiple short runs).
- Internal: Aditya/Vivek/Rishi — I'll loop you in to define test harness and pass/fail thresholds.

Attachments: clearsky-throughput-samples-20261101.csv, slo-targets-qa-20261101.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to locking down the sizing and a short validation window.

—

Thanks Lauren — great summary and thanks for the clear next steps. Quick answers inline and I've attached a small sample of production traces (sanitized).

Inline answers:
1) Token histograms: attached CSV contains 90 days of anonymized request/response token counts. Median response ~96 tokens; 95th ~220.
2) Traffic shape: baseline weekday steady-state ~6–8 req/s, with predictable daily peaks up to ~28 req/s; rare bursts during launches up to ~45 req/s (10–15min windows). Concurrent open streams: 320 typical, 60–80 truly active streaming sessions at any given second during peaks.
3) Network: requests originate in us-west, we terminate TLS at a Cloud Load Balancer in our VPC; internal RTT adds ~8–12ms average.

Operational constraints:
- We want the option to keep keys within our KMS (private deployment) — not mandatory for initial run but planned before go-live.
- Budget guardrails: initial reserved commit target is 3 GPUs; we can expand after evidence.

Attached: clearsky-prod-sample-traces-20261101.csv

Happy to sync if you want to walk the trace file together.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: dedicated capacity sizing for low-latency streaming

Looping through Nora's numbers — good data. A few quick back-of-envelope calculations and a proposed carve: 

What the numbers imply (rough):
- Peak sustainable request rate to plan for: 45 req/s (burst). With avg response ~120 tokens and avg prompt ~48 tokens, that's ~7,560 tokens/s (45 * 168 tokens) or ~453,600 tokens/min.
- Active streaming sessions: 60–80 truly active streams -> we must validate concurrent KV/attention memory behavior (prefixs + KV for streaming).

GPU sizing tradeoffs (short):
- H100: highest single-GPU throughput, best for long sequences and streaming tail. Good for keeping p95 low under high concurrency due to tensor core perf and NVLink setups. Higher cost; best if KV/cache needs are high and if they want fewer reserved units.
- A100 80GB: balanced option for general-purpose (good memory headroom for KV); slightly cheaper than H100 when amortized.
- L40: cost-efficient for int8 quantized variants; we will likely need more instances to hit the same tail-latency / concurrency numbers but can be cheaper overall if model quantization is acceptable.

Recommended initial reserved pools (hypothesis):
- Conservative (quality-first): 3 x H100 (reserve) — should hit p95 < 250ms for 120–256 token responses in our internal runs, assuming NVLink and local network within their VPC.
- Cost-first (quantized path): 6 x L40 (int8) — less headroom for tail but cheaper; run validation with int8 model to check quality regressions.

Validation plan (detailed):
1) Baseline: run 30-min steady-state at 30 req/s + 15-min spike to 45 req/s, measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming end-to-end (client-facing).
2) Tail/kv: targeted tests for 60/80 concurrent streaming sessions with long-lived KV (simulate 5–10k token sessions).
3) Cold-start tests (scale from 0 -> target) and graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model variant).
4) Repeat with quantized model (int8) on L40 to check quality/perf delta.

Deliverables after run: latency breakdown (network vs runtime), token/sec throughput, resource utilization per GPU, recommended final reserved commit and suggested fallback (model variant + routing policy).

Proposed timing: run the first validation Thu 2026-11-04 morning (US/PST). I'll own the harness and put a concise pass/fail sheet together.
